thread_text:
lucy: FYI customer reports 403 on embeddings endpoint, thinks it's an invalid API key. they pasted the error: `{"error":"invalid_api_key"}`. customer insists key is valid and shows plan is Pro in their dashboard. can we check?

mike: thanks — can you paste the exact curl they ran (redact key) and any response headers? 403 alone is ambiguous.

lucy: sure. they ran:```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-redwood_ABC...REDACTED\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"input":"hello"}'```response headers:```HTTP/2 403
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: r-9f3b2
server: redwood-inference
```and body was `{"error":"invalid_api_key"}` per their screenshot. they also sent their account id: acct_93X and screenshot of billing UI showing plan: Team Pro, seats 10.

sam: quick lookup on acct_93X: billing shows the plan row flagged as "payment_failed" 2026-11-02 invoice inv_20261102 attached, the plan was auto-suspended last week. system sets entitlement=inactive when invoice unpaid. that would trigger the entitlement gate, which currently returns 403 with the same top-level error shape we use for auth failures. note: we don't surface a distinct error code in the body.

lucy: ah ok so customer sees "invalid_api_key" and believes key is wrong. they escalated to support. can we change messaging? even a different error message would help.

mike: agreed. this is a recurring confusion — entitlement gating (billing/feature flags) and auth failures both return 403 w/ ambiguous body. eng-runtime: can we augment the response to include an `error.code` like `entitlement_blocked` and a header `x-rd-error-reason: entitlement`? small change but will unblock support triage.

sam: technically trivial. patch path: middleware that maps entitlement check failures currently throws generic `AuthError(403, "invalid_api_key")`. we can change the constructor to set `error.code = \"entitlement_blocked\"` and include header. will open a canary PR.

lucy: ✅ customer needs a temporary workaround — what's the quickest step we can ask them to try so they can resume service?

sam: short-term: customer should verify billing/payment method or retry invoice. I've re-sent the failed invoice link to acct_93X (I can do that). Also we can ask them to call the admin that manages billing to restore plan. long-term we should not conflate reasons.

mike: also note SSO/OAuth flows: if a customer uses SSO and their org lost entitlement, the client often sees the same error. any chance to provide a more actionable message in the response body, e.g., "error": {"code":"entitlement_blocked","message":"account suspended: invoice unpaid", "help_url":"https://console.redwood.ai/billing"}?

sam: yep. will propose body change. adding header is faster and safe. body change needs docs and SDK bumps.

nina-billing-bot: automated note: invoice inv_20261102 for acct_93X status=failed, amount=$2,400. retry link sent to billing@acct_93X.

lucy: I told customer to check billing email and to share a payment txn if they re-run it. they asked if we can whitelist them temporarily so they can finish a demo tomorrow. can we do that?

sam: we can temporarily flip entitlement flag for acct_93X from `suspended`->`active` in internal console for up to 24h. need an approval from billing ops. @billing-ops please ack.

mike: action items: 1) sam to open canary PR that adds `x-rd-error-reason: entitlement` header and `error.code` in body for entitlement blocks; 2) support (lucy) to ask customer to confirm payment or accept temporary enable if billing ops approves; 3) billing ops to follow up on inv_20261102.

sam: PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/mercury/pulls/459 — patch adds header + body code for entitlement cases and unit tests. will request canary deploy to staging.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for pr 459 on staging. ETA ~ 12m.

lucy: perfect. I'll keep the thread updated. customer says they can wait 12m for a clearer error but still wants a manual unblock if billing ops can approve.

mike: long-term follow-up: we should audit all 403s and enumerate whether they are auth, rate-limit, entitlement, or policy denials. create a tiny RFC? I'll write one and post in #eng-runtime.

lucy: thanks all. marking this as escalated -> billing-review. I'll thread back with the customer once billing confirms. :thumbsup:

sam: update: staging canary returned entitlement responses with header and `{"error":{"code":"entitlement_blocked","message":"account suspended: payment failed"}}` — looks good. planning to ship to prod after 1h of monitoring.

lucy: copied to customer. they appreciated the clearer message. closing after billing ops either reinstates or confirms suspension.

mike: small note for docs/devex: add FAQ entry 'Why do I get 403 if my key is valid?' linking to billing and plan status.

lucy: noted. I'll add a support KB draft and ping docs.

-- thread end --
